name: Separate linked functions through selective dissociation
description: Seek comparisons preserving one property while changing another. Use their dissociation to distinguish a required functional relation from amount, delivery, stability or another linked activity.
use_when: A mutant phenotype is assigned to one molecular function despite several potentially affected properties.
live_alternatives: Distinct connections jointly contribute but can reside on different molecules.
The measured activity and native role dissociate.
decision_guidance: Prefer positive evidence that alternative properties survive; a failed construct is not automatically selective.
Reciprocal/complementary contrasts are informative when their predicted results differ, without requiring them universally.
Keep incomplete perturbation validation as a limit rather than claiming a specific null from its label.

outcome_contingencies.then_consider: Exclude simple instability/mislocalization without inventing direct binding.

outcome_contingencies.if_observed: Complementary defects restore function but same-defect controls do not
outcome_contingencies.then_consider: Support joint contribution of distinct connections.

outcome_contingencies.if_observed: Endpoint survives a supposed catalytic-null mutation without null validation
outcome_contingencies.then_consider: Do not infer catalytic dispensability from the label.

boundary: This is an inference pattern, not mutagenesis instructions. P02 tests predictors and can use natural variation; P17 adds causal perturbation selectivity. Ordinary suppressors are not reciprocal separation-of-function evidence.

evidence.source_locator: Case-record observation; inspected scope: Primary full Results examined, including mutant fold/function controls and the mixed-complex repair experiment.
evidence.observation: DnaA- or DnaN-interaction defects complemented in trans with same-defect controls, restoring foci/initiation control.
evidence.limit: The result does not settle every molecular YabA model.
